# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and analyzer from crashing on closed generic structs that come from a referenced assembly. Two places that read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` now tolerate an empty list. Every diagnostic the analyzer reports now passes through a new filter, `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, which drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the current compilation. Three tests compile a library to metadata and check that the consuming project builds without warnings and gets its resolver. Two doc sections are added.
story.why: Issue #2283: for metadata types `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so indexing `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. The generator then produced no resolver at all.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global filter on all analyzer diagnostics: any diagnostic with no in-compilation source location is now silently dropped, not just ones caused by metadata types.
`GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` uses `as` instead of a hard cast, which changes behavior for non-`PropertyDeclarationSyntax` declarations in source.
README and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md text, and the two docs contradict each other.
story.confidence_overview: High that the two edited index sites no longer throw. Medium that the crash is fully fixed: the issue names three indexing sites and only two are visibly changed. Medium on whether the tests cover the analyzer as well as the generator. Low on the docs: MsgPack004.md describes behavior the code does not have.

refusals.what: Analyzer diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are now suppressed, and any diagnostic without an in-compilation source location is dropped.
refusals.why: This changes which user-visible analyzer diagnostics fire. That is a product decision, not a crash fix, and S4 only checks descriptors.

refusals.what: Documentation added beyond the requirement, with MsgPack004.md stating behavior the code does not implement and contradicting README.
refusals.why: These are changes beyond the requirement, and the docs misdescribe the behavior.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: Neither named test exercises BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (TypeCollector.cs:983-986) or GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (TypeCollector.cs:1434), because every Key attribute in ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference (GenericsFormatterTests.cs:517) and ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference (GenericsFormatterTests.cs:559) uses integer key 0 (intKey != null). Also, the quoted requirement identifies three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites in GetObjectInfo (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in v3.1.8, corresponding to ~711, 985, 1077 with the 24-line offset), and the diff updates only two of them.

The doc says members of a referenced-assembly type are reported in the consuming project at the using member. The code does the opposite: `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` drops them, and README line 1642 says they are reported only by the defining assembly. The two docs contradict each other, and MsgPack004.md is false.

The filter applies to every analyzer diagnostic, not only metadata-member ones. Any existing diagnostic created with a null/Location.None location for a source type is now silently suppressed. This could hide real MsgPack00x reports that previously surfaced.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in 3.1.8). Only two are visibly changed in this diff. If a third direct index remains elsewhere in `GetObjectInfo`, another metadata path could still throw. Check with a grep for `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`.

The hard cast was replaced with `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. For a source property declared as a positional record parameter (ParameterSyntax), BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull now gets a null location and is silently dropped by the filter, instead of being reported.

An unkeyed public member on a metadata type is no longer reported in the consumer. The generator may still emit or assume a formatter for that type, with no warning anywhere if the defining assembly did not run the analyzer (for example, a third-party package).

MsgPack004.md lines 51-52 claim that unattributed public members of types defined in referenced assemblies are reported in the consuming project at the member that uses the type, which is the exact opposite of the implemented behavior: TypeCollector.cs:1077 locates MemberNeedsKey on the member itself (null/Location.None for metadata), ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (TypeCollector.cs:239, 1446) drops it, README.md:1642 states consuming projects do not report it, and ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember (GenericsFormatterTests.cs:590-626) asserts zero diagnostics.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops any diagnostic with !diagnostic.Location.IsInSource, silently suppressing valid diagnostics on symbols in the current compilation whenever a location helper returns null (Location.None). In particular, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (line 1434) casts syntax via 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', which returns null for positional record/record struct primary-constructor properties (ParameterSyntax) and indexers (IndexerDeclarationSyntax), so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) on a positional record property in the current compilation gets Location.None and is silently dropped; the same applies to diagnostics using GetParameterListLocation (line 1454) on implicitly declared constructors.

REQ-2283 identified three direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing sites inside GetObjectInfo (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in v3.1.8). Accounting for the 24-line offset (1009 -> 985 and 1101 -> 1077), only two were fixed; the remaining site around line 711 is untouched and will still throw IndexOutOfRangeException if a metadata closed generic value type hits that diagnostic path.
